title: Read-only gate refuses ordinary Git object inspection in evaluators: `git cat-file -t` and `<rev>^{tree}`
outcome: A read-only evaluator or reviewer can inspect Git objects and trees the ordinary way, while commands that can run external programs or change state stay refused.
acceptance: The read-only Git rule admits `git cat-file` with `-t`, `-s`, `-e` or `-p` on an object, and keeps refusing `--textconv`, `--filters` and the batch modes.

Revision arguments using `^{tree}`, `^{commit}` and similar peel syntax are admitted in read-only Git commands such as `git rev-parse <rev>^{tree}`, without admitting shell brace expansion that runs anything.
Behaviour tests cover each admitted form and each still-refused form.
